fr-b01-n01: Japanese gives every kana equal length and rides on pitch, not stress. Six moves, and half-known words start landing.
fr-b01-n02: Your hand does this: one even tap per kana, same size, gliding flat. English bumps one syllable; Japanese never does.
fr-b01-n03: Move one: every kana is one equal beat. Ko-o-hi-i is four beats, not KOFF-ee. Tap them level as you say it.
fr-b01-t01: すみません、コーヒーをお願いします。
fr-b01-p01: At the counter, open with sumimasen and then order one coffee. Speak now.
fr-b01-p02: She hands it over. Thank her, and let the u at the end go almost silent. Speak now.
fr-b01-t02: ありがとうございます。
fr-b01-n04: Move two: the five vowels are pure and never glide. A is ah, i is ee, u is oo, e is eh, o is oh — the same every time.
fr-b01-t03: ホテルまでお願いします。
fr-b01-p03: You get into a taxi with the address already on your phone. Tell him where. Speak now.
fr-b01-p04: The board just changed and you need the new departure time. Speak now.
fr-b01-n05: Move three: a long vowel is a real second beat that changes the word. Biru is a building, biiru is a beer — one beat longer.
fr-b01-r01: ビル、ビール。おばさん、おばあさん。
fr-b01-p05: At the bakery, ask for one bread. Give each kana its own beat. Speak now.
fr-b01-n06: Move four: the little tsu is a held silent beat. In kitte or kippu, hold one silent beat, then release.
fr-b01-t06: 切符を二枚お願いします。
fr-b01-p06: Same counter, at the ticket window. Order two, and hold the little stop in the middle of kippu. Speak now.
fr-b01-n07: Move five: i and u go nearly silent between soft consonants. Desu is dess, sukiyaki starts skiyaki. Written, not sounded.
fr-b01-p07: She asks whether you want anything else. Close the order — that is all. Speak now.
fr-b01-t07: 以上です。ありがとうございます。
fr-b01-p08: You are inside a café and you need the back of the room. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b01-n08: Move six: r is a light tap between English r, l and d; accent is a pitch drop, not loudness — words slide past edgeless.
fr-b01-p09: The shutter is half up and someone is moving about inside. Ask before you walk in. Speak now.
fr-b01-t09: すみません、開いていますか？
fr-b01-s01: すみません、コーヒーをお願いします。パンをください。トイレはどこですか？ ありがとうございます。
fr-b01-n09: B01 done. One beat per kana, five pure vowels, long vowels held, little tsu silent, i and u dropped, pitch not stress.
fr-b01-q-i: A traveller orders at a counter and then asks for the back of the room.
fr-b01-q01: すみません、コーヒーをお願いします。
fr-b01-q03: 以上です。ありがとうございます。
fr-b01-q04: トイレは奥の右側です。
fr-b02-n01: Ten words cover a whole shop. One opens the visit, one closes it, and one isn't yours — the greeting staff aim at you.
fr-b02-p01: You are crossing into a small shop with the owner behind the counter. Speak now.
fr-b02-n02: The greeting shifts with the hour. Morning's full warm form is ohayou gozaimasu — the gozaimasu makes it polite.
fr-b02-p02: Early morning, at the bakery, and the woman behind the counter looks up at you. Speak now.
fr-b02-p03: It is dark outside and you are walking into a restaurant where a man is holding the door. Speak now.
fr-b02-n03: No exact hour turns konnichiwa into konbanwa — it goes by the light and the room. Copy whichever one reaches you.
fr-b02-p04: He tilts the bottle towards your glass for a second one, and you want it. Speak now.
fr-b02-p05: You are browsing and someone offers to help. Turn it down without closing the door. Speak now.
fr-b02-r02: はい、どうぞごゆっくり。
fr-b02-n04: English is limited here — read it as a direction, not a count: some at hotels, stations and airports, far less at a small shop.
fr-b02-p06: She has just wrapped the thing and handed it across. Speak now.
fr-b02-t06: ありがとうございます。
fr-b02-p07: The aisle is narrow and your bag has just caught someone's arm. Speak now.
fr-b02-n05: On its own, sumimasen covers a bump or a squeeze past. Next part, it opens anything you need from a stranger.
fr-b02-p08: You are at the door on your way out and he is still behind the counter. Speak now.
fr-b02-t08: ありがとうございました。
fr-b02-p09: You have just finished eating and you are getting up to leave. Say the thing people say after a meal here. Speak now.
fr-b02-r03: ありがとうございました。またお越しくださいませ。
fr-b02-s01: こんにちは。はい、お願いします。ありがとうございます。ごちそうさまでした。
fr-b02-n06: B02 done. Greeting in, gozaimasu, hai and iie, arigatou, sumimasen, arigatou gozaimashita and gochisousama out — irasshaimase is theirs.
fr-b02-q-i: A traveller walks into a small shop, buys one thing and leaves.
fr-b02-q03: はい、お願いします。ありがとうございます。
fr-b02-q04: ありがとうございました。またお越しくださいませ。
fr-b03-n01: You will lose a sentence on day one. That is not something to avoid — it is a moment with one opener that fixes it.
fr-b03-n02: The frame: sumimasen, then the thing you need. Same opener for the clerk, the station staff and the person in the doorway.
fr-b03-t01: すみません、わかりませんでした。
fr-b03-p01: At the konbini counter she has just said a number and it went straight past you. Speak now.
fr-b03-r01: あ、失礼しました。二百四十円です。
fr-b03-n03: The frame holds and only the ending changes: ask for it again, ask for it slower, ask for it written down.
fr-b03-p02: Same counter, and one more go at it would settle everything. Speak now.
fr-b03-t02: すみません、もう一度お願いします。
fr-b03-p03: At the ticket window the repeat came back at the same speed. Ask for the other thing. Speak now.
fr-b03-t03: すみません、ゆっくりお願いします。
fr-b03-p04: Still at the ticket window, and it is a platform number you cannot afford to guess. Speak now.
fr-b03-t04: すみません、書いてもらえますか？
fr-b03-n04: One word does three jobs: sumimasen calls attention, apologises, and can even thank. You never change it for who you're talking to.
fr-b03-p05: The train is packed and your stop is next. Speak now.
fr-b03-n05: Two more endings for the frame, both used on the street: the time, and whether the person has English.
fr-b03-p06: On the street outside, phone dead, and someone is waiting at the crossing. Speak now.
fr-b03-t06: すみません、今何時ですか？
fr-b03-p07: Same street, and what you need next is longer than your Japanese. Open properly first. Speak now.
fr-b03-t07: すみません、英語は話せますか？
fr-b03-r03: 少しなら。何をお探しですか？
fr-b03-p08: Back at the konbini counter, holding up the thing you want to be able to name. Speak now.
fr-b03-t08: すみません、これは日本語で何と言いますか？
fr-b03-p09: Same counter, pointing at the tray you cannot identify. Speak now.
fr-b03-t09: すみません、これは何ですか？
fr-b03-p10: They slowed down, repeated it and wrote the number on the receipt. Close it warmly. Speak now.
fr-b03-t10: ありがとうございます。助かりました。
fr-b03-s01: すみません、わかりませんでした。すみません、もう一度お願いします。すみません、ゆっくりお願いします。すみません、通ります。
fr-b03-n06: B03 done. Sumimasen plus the need covers the repeat, the slow version, the written version, the way through and the time.
fr-b03-q-i: A traveller loses a price at a counter and gets it back in three moves.
fr-b03-q01: すみません、わかりませんでした。
fr-b03-q02: あ、失礼しました。二百四十円です。
fr-b03-q03: すみません、ゆっくりお願いします。
fr-b03-q04: 二百、四十円です。はい、どうぞ。
fr-b04-n01: Tonight's list is short and it expires. Four things, all cheaper to fix at home than at a counter in Japan.
fr-b04-n02: One: travel insurance with medical cover. Japan has no reciprocal scheme, so a visitor pays the full bill up front. No European card helps.
fr-b04-n03: Two: the transport card. A chip shortage stopped plain Suica sales — get a Welcome Suica at the airport, or Suica on your phone.
fr-b04-n04: Three: cash. Decide the amount now — foreign cards only work in some ATMs here, reliably the ones at 7-Eleven and Japan Post.
fr-b04-n05: Four: the booking, saved where no signal is needed. Full address in Japanese, phone number, return ticket.
fr-b04-r01: はい、ホテルさくら、でございます。
fr-b04-p01: You are ringing the hotel a week before the flight. Open with the job, in one line. Speak now.
fr-b04-t01: 予約の確認をお願いしたいのですが。
fr-b04-n06: A hotel name is not a destination. A driver and an offline map both need the address — Japanese addresses go by block, not street.
fr-b04-p02: The booking page shows a brand name and a district. Get the thing a driver can actually navigate to. Speak now.
fr-b04-t02: 住所を教えてもらえますか？
fr-b04-r02: 中央区銀座一丁目二番三号です。
fr-b04-p03: You will not hold that in your head, and a green tick in an app is not proof. Ask for it another way. Speak now.
fr-b04-t03: メールで送ってもらえますか？
fr-b04-n07: Late arrival is the one detail worth saying out loud. Small front desks are not always staffed at night.
fr-b04-p04: Your flight lands at nine and the train takes an hour. Tell them when to expect you. Speak now.
fr-b04-t04: 夜の十時ごろ着きます。
fr-b04-p05: Now check that somebody will be standing there when you push the door. Speak now.
fr-b04-t05: その時間、フロントは開いていますか？
fr-b04-r03: はい、フロントは二十四時間開いております。
fr-b04-p06: Before you decide how much cash to bring, find out how this place wants to be paid. Speak now.
fr-b04-p07: Get something you can dial from a payphone at arrivals if the handset is dead. Speak now.
fr-b04-t07: ホテルの電話番号を教えてください。
fr-b04-p08: Close the call the way it opened — warm, and finished. Speak now.
fr-b04-t08: わかりました。ありがとうございます。よろしくお願いします。
fr-b04-s01: 予約の確認をお願いしたいのですが。住所を教えてもらえますか？ メールで送ってもらえますか？
fr-b04-n08: B04 done. Insurance bought, transport card planned, cash decided, booking confirmed with an address in hand.
fr-b04-q-i: A traveller closes the gaps in a booking a week before departure.
fr-b04-q01: 予約の確認をお願いしたいのですが。
fr-b04-q02: 中央区銀座一丁目二番三号です。
fr-b04-q03: メールで送ってもらえますか？
fr-b04-q04: はい、メールでお送りします。
fr-b05-n01: The desk is three questions, not a Japanese exam. Why you came, how long, where you sleep.
fr-b05-r01: こんにちは。旅行の目的は何ですか？
fr-b05-p01: You are here to walk around, eat well and go home. Say it in one word. Speak now.
fr-b05-n02: Use your own number, not the one in this lesson. The shape stays exactly as short either way.
fr-b05-p02: Give the length of the stay and nothing else. Two words. Speak now.
fr-b05-n03: Not the story of how you found the place. City, kind of place, full stop.
fr-b05-p03: Say where you sleep, briefly — the city and the kind of place. Speak now.
fr-b05-p04: Hand over the offline copy you saved last night, and let the document do the talking. Speak now.
fr-b05-n04: Kore desu is the entire sentence. Three syllables and an open hand outrun any paragraph.
fr-b05-n05: If you did not catch the question, say so once and plainly. Asking beats guessing at a desk.
fr-b05-p05: It went past you too fast. Say so cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
fr-b05-t05: すみません、わかりませんでした。
fr-b05-p06: Nobody is with you on this trip. Say it in three words. Speak now.
fr-b05-t06: 一人で旅行しています。
fr-b05-p07: They ask whether you are seeing anywhere else. Answer truthfully and briefly. Speak now.
fr-b05-t07: その後、京都に行きます。
fr-b05-r05: はい、大丈夫です。良いご旅行を。
fr-b05-p08: Three words, take the passport, walk. Speak now.
fr-b05-t08: ありがとうございます。
fr-b05-s01: 観光です。十日間です。東京の、ホテルです。はい、これです。
fr-b05-n06: B05 done. Purpose, length, place, kore desu. Short is not evasive — short means the answer matched the question.
fr-b05-q-i: A traveller clears the border desk in four short answers.
fr-b05-q01: こんにちは。旅行の目的は何ですか？
fr-b05-q04: 東京の、ホテルです。はい、これです。
fr-b06-n01: Your first hour is four counters and four small questions. In Japan they all end the same way.
fr-b06-n02: Here is the frame: the thing, then wa arimasu ka. Do you have — and does it even exist here.
fr-b06-t01: すみません、ワイファイはありますか？
fr-b06-p01: At the airport café, your eSIM still has not connected and you need the network. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-r01: はい、パスワードはレシートに書いてあります。
fr-b06-n03: Notice what the frame asks: not the grammar, just whether this place has the thing. The particle wa and the ending arimasu ka never change.
fr-b06-p02: At the phone shop past the gates, you want a local number for the week. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-n04: Sumimasen comes first, every single time. Arriving with the request and no sumimasen is entering without knocking.
fr-b06-p03: Back at the phone shop, your battery is at four percent and yours is in the hold. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-p04: At the konbini by the exit you want an IC card for the trains, and the machines have a long queue. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-n05: The frame does not care what the thing is. Wifi, a SIM, a charger, an IC card, change, a map.
fr-b06-n06: Cash is still king here. Small places may be cash only, while konbini and stations take cards and Suica.
fr-b06-p05: The drinks machine at the airport café takes coins only and all you have is a note. Ask at the konbini. Speak now.
fr-b06-r02: いいえ、ここにはありませんが、二階にありますよ。
fr-b06-n07: A no usually comes with the address of the yes attached. Stay one beat past the iie.
fr-b06-p06: At the information desk, paper survives a flat battery and your battery is nearly flat. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-p07: Back at the airport café, before the train and the long ride into town. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b06-p08: They sorted you out in ten seconds. Close it the way people close things here. Speak now.
fr-b06-t08: どうもありがとうございます。
fr-b06-s01: ワイファイはありますか？ SIMカードはありますか？ 小銭はありますか？
fr-b06-n08: B06 done. One frame, four counters, and the whole first hour answered with a noun and wa arimasu ka.
fr-b06-q-i: A traveller crosses the arrivals hall with one opening and seven different needs.
fr-b06-q01: すみません、ワイファイはありますか？
fr-b06-q02: はい、パスワードはレシートに書いてあります。
fr-b06-q04: いいえ、ここにはありませんが、二階にありますよ。
fr-b07-n01: Between the plane and the bed there are four counters, and each one has its own rule about what you may do there.
fr-b07-n02: The frame: action in te-form, then te mo ii desu ka — may I, then the job. The ending never moves; learn the verb already in te-form.
fr-b07-t01: カードで払ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-p01: You are at the ticket machine in arrivals and the only notes in your pocket are the wrong currency. Ask before you queue. Speak now.
fr-b07-r01: すみません、うちは現金のみなんです。
fr-b07-n03: No business here must take a card; many small places are cash-only. Konbini, chains and transport take cards and IC; yen always works.
fr-b07-p02: Same machine, and the sign says cash only. You have coins and notes. Offer the other way. Speak now.
fr-b07-t02: 現金で払ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-p03: You are at a small counter and you cannot tell whether it sells anything or only gives information. Speak now.
fr-b07-t03: ここで切符を買ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-r02: はい、あちらの券売機でも買えますよ。
fr-b07-n04: Same opener, different problem. You change the action in front of it and nothing else.
fr-b07-p04: The train to town is at the platform, the doors are narrow and you have a big case beside you. Check with the agent. Speak now.
fr-b07-t04: 荷物を持って乗ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-p05: The taxi has stopped at your hotel and you have just paid. There is a piece of paper the driver owes you. Ask for it. Speak now.
fr-b07-t05: 領収書をもらってもいいですか？
fr-b07-r03: はい、どうぞ。空港からは定額なんですよ。
fr-b07-n05: Some airport runs have a fixed fare to ask for; otherwise the meter. Either way, no tipping, and the receipt is yours for the asking.
fr-b07-p06: You reach the hotel desk four hours before the room is ready and you would like your hands back. Speak now.
fr-b07-t06: ここに荷物を置いてもいいですか？
fr-b07-p07: There is one free armchair in the hotel lobby and someone's coat on the next one. Check first. Speak now.
fr-b07-t07: ここに座ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-p08: Four percent of battery, the booking is on the screen, and there is a socket behind the desk. Speak now.
fr-b07-t08: ここで充電してもいいですか？
fr-b07-p09: The carriage is packed, your stop is next and there are three people between you and the door. Speak now.
fr-b07-p10: The driver got you to the door and it is late. Say the two things you say on the way out. Speak now.
fr-b07-t10: ありがとうございます。おやすみなさい。
fr-b07-s01: カードで払ってもいいですか？ 荷物を持って乗ってもいいですか？ ここに荷物を置いてもいいですか？
fr-b07-n06: B07 done. The frame covered the machine, the platform, the taxi, the desk and the seat — one ending, nine actions.
fr-b07-q-i: A traveller crosses four counters between the plane and the bed with one opening.
fr-b07-q01: カードで払ってもいいですか？
fr-b07-q02: すみません、うちは現金のみなんです。
fr-b07-q03: 領収書をもらってもいいですか？
fr-b07-q04: はい、どうぞ。空港からは定額なんですよ。
fr-b08-n01: Asking is the easy half. The hard half is getting back an answer short enough to still be in your head at the corner.
fr-b08-n02: Here is the frame: the place, then wa doko desu ka. The place is the only thing you choose; the ending never moves.
fr-b08-t01: すみません、駅はどこですか？
fr-b08-p01: You have twenty minutes before a train and no idea which way the tracks are. Open, then ask. Speak now.
fr-b08-r01: 二つ目の角を右に曲がって、まっすぐです。ここから五分くらいですよ。
fr-b08-n03: That came back faster than you can hold. So ask again in a shape that only allows a yes, a no or a hand.
fr-b08-p02: You caught about half of that. Point down one street and make them confirm or correct you. Speak now.
fr-b08-r02: はい、そうです。まっすぐです。
fr-b08-p03: You are underground in a station hall with corridors going four ways and no daylight anywhere. Speak now.
fr-b08-p04: It is raining, you are outside the station, and cabs keep passing without stopping because they load at one spot. Speak now.
fr-b08-t04: タクシー乗り場はどこですか？
fr-b08-n04: The place you will ask for most has two names: toire, and the politer otearai. Either one finds it, and it is the one you tend to ask in a hurry.
fr-b08-p05: You are inside a café and the back of the room has three unmarked doors. Ask the person at the counter. Speak now.
fr-b08-p06: They have pointed. Now find out whether this is a two-minute walk or a bus ride, in three sounds. Speak now.
fr-b08-r03: いいえ、歩いて五分です。
fr-b08-p07: You have walked the whole side of the museum and every door so far has said groups only. Speak now.
fr-b08-p08: At the museum ticket desk. Your phone is dead and there is a stack of folded paper behind the counter. Speak now.
fr-b08-n05: And when it comes back too fast, you have one line that buys you the whole answer again, slower.
fr-b08-p09: The whole reply went past you in about two seconds. Ask for it again. Speak now.
fr-b08-t09: すみません、もう一度お願いします。
fr-b08-s01: 駅はどこですか？ 出口はどこですか？ こっちですか？ 遠いですか？
fr-b08-n06: B08 done. The frame found the station, the exit, the rank, the toilet and the entrance — and two follow-ups kept the answers portable.
fr-b08-q-i: A traveller asks for a place, gets thirty words back, and makes them fit.
fr-b08-q01: すみません、駅はどこですか？
fr-b08-q02: 二つ目の角を右に曲がって、まっすぐです。
fr-b08-q03: こっちですか？遠いですか？
fr-b08-q04: いいえ、歩いて五分です。
fr-b09-n01: Buying the ticket is the simple part. What varies is whether one ticket is enough, or this train wants a second.
fr-b09-p01: You have a basic ticket and the train at the platform is a fast one. Ask the agent by the gate before you board. Speak now.
fr-b09-r01: 新幹線は要ります。でも普通電車なら要りませんよ。
fr-b09-n02: On JR a Shinkansen or limited express needs two tickets: fare plus limited-express. A local or rapid needs only the fare or IC.
fr-b09-n03: If the exit gate won't open, you're not fined — you underpaid. Settle it at the fare-adjustment machine before the gate.
fr-b09-p02: You have reached the exit and the gate flap stayed shut — your IC ran short. Find the machine that fixes it. Speak now.
fr-b09-p03: At the ticket window. One traveller, and the name you want on the board is Kyoto. Keep it to the destination and the courtesy. Speak now.
fr-b09-t03: 京都まで一枚お願いします。
fr-b09-r02: 十二番線、十四時三十五分発です。
fr-b09-n04: Times come on the twenty-four hour clock. Juuyoji sanjuugofun is twenty-five to three in the afternoon.
fr-b09-p04: You have the number but the concourse signs jump from nine to fifteen. Speak now.
fr-b09-t04: 十二番線はどこですか？
fr-b09-p05: Two trains are standing at the same platform and the display is showing neither. Check with the person by the door. Speak now.
fr-b09-t05: この電車は京都に行きますか？
fr-b09-r03: はい、でも新大阪で乗り換えです。
fr-b09-p06: You heard a station name you were not expecting in the middle of that. Turn it into a yes or a no. Speak now.
fr-b09-t06: 乗り換えが必要ですか？
fr-b09-n05: On a fast train, cars are non-reserved or reserved. The surcharge seats you non-reserved; a reserved seat costs a bit more.
fr-b09-p07: The machines in this hall all show a queue and a screen you cannot read from here. You want the staffed JR office. Speak now.
fr-b09-t07: みどりの窓口はどこですか？
fr-b09-p08: First morning in Japan, ten days ahead of you, and you would rather tap one card than feed paper into every gate. Speak now.
fr-b09-t08: ウェルカムスイカをお願いします。
fr-b09-p09: You are off the train, underground, and the corridors go four ways. Speak now.
fr-b09-s01: 特急券は要りますか？ 精算機はどこですか？ この電車は京都に行きますか？ 乗り換えが必要ですか？
fr-b09-n06: B09 done. Tokkyuuken, the fare machine, the platform, the train and the change — four minutes, five questions.
fr-b09-q-i: A traveller settles a platform in four minutes and five questions.
fr-b09-q02: 新幹線は要ります。でも普通電車なら要りませんよ。
fr-b09-q03: 十二番線はどこですか？
fr-b09-q04: 十二番線、十四時三十五分発です。
fr-b10-n01: Japan writes many signs in katakana, in words you think you know. Most are friendly. A few send you to the wrong place.
fr-b10-n02: The frame: the thing, then wo sagashite imasu — I'm looking for. The trap: a マンション is no mansion, just an apartment block.
fr-b10-p01: You need a proper pharmacy for a prescription, not just a shelf of drinks. Say what you are after. Speak now.
fr-b10-r01: 薬局ですか？ この先のドラッグストアにもありますよ。
fr-b10-n03: Keep the frame, change the thing. And watch サービス: from a shopkeeper or receipt it means free, on the house — not a charge.
fr-b10-p02: Your wallet is empty and the only machine you passed refused a foreign card. Open the search at the counter. Speak now.
fr-b10-t02: エーティーエムを探しています。
fr-b10-r02: コンビニのエーティーエムなら海外のカードも使えますよ。すぐそこです。
fr-b10-p03: The card went through and you want to be sure there was no hidden fee. Say what you have, plainly. Speak now.
fr-b10-t03: すみません、現金しかないんです。
fr-b10-n04: コンセント is a power socket, not consent. Asking where the コンセント is means where can I plug in, nothing more.
fr-b10-p04: Every door on this side of the building is marked 出口, exit. Ask for the other one. Speak now.
fr-b10-n05: The convenience store answers half these searches. Three big chains pass fifty-five thousand branches, most open all hours.
fr-b10-p05: The small restaurant looks open but the lights are half down and it is three in the afternoon. Ask about the gap in the hours. Speak now.
fr-b10-r03: はい、二時から五時まで休憩です。夜は五時からです。
fr-b10-n06: ビル is a building, not a bill. And バイキング on a restaurant sign is an all-you-can-eat buffet, nothing to do with Vikings.
fr-b10-p06: At the drugstore counter, you have a dry cough and no idea what the box is called. Speak now.
fr-b10-t06: 咳の薬を探しています。
fr-b10-n07: クレーム is a complaint, not a cream. If a sign points to the クレーム counter, that is where problems go, not desserts.
fr-b10-p07: There is a socket on the wall by your table and your phone is at four percent. Ask whether you may use it. Speak now.
fr-b10-t07: ここで充電してもいいですか？
fr-b10-n08: For cash, use the konbini or post office, not the bank. Their machines take foreign cards in English, all hours; banks often won't.
fr-b10-p08: Someone is inside with the lights on and the shutter still down. Open politely and ask about opening time. Speak now.
fr-b10-t08: すみません、何時に開きますか？
fr-b10-p09: You are holding what you chose and there are three counters, none obviously the paying one. Speak now.
fr-b10-p10: Someone steps towards you the moment you walk in and you have not decided anything. Speak now.
fr-b10-t10: ちょっと見てもいいですか？
fr-b10-s01: 薬局を探しています。入口はどこですか？ お昼は休憩ですか？
fr-b10-n09: B10 done. マンション, サービス, コンセント, ビル, バイキング — five katakana words that now say what they actually say.
fr-b10-q-i: A traveller reads three lines of katakana, hears one word that lies, and opens a search before trusting the resemblance.
fr-b10-q01: すみません、薬局を探しています。
fr-b10-q02: 薬局ですか？ この先のドラッグストアにもありますよ。
fr-b10-q03: 開いていますか？ お昼は休憩ですか？
fr-b10-q04: 今は休憩です。二時から開きます。
fr-b11-n01: The first round is where pointing stops working. One ending does the ordering, and it is already the polite one.
fr-b11-n02: The frame is the thing, then onegai shimasu. Name it — a coffee, the menu, the water — and onegai shimasu does the courtesy.
fr-b11-t01: コーヒーをお願いします。
fr-b11-p01: You are at the counter, it is nine in the morning, and it is your turn. Speak now.
fr-b11-r01: コーヒーですね。店内でお召し上がりですか？
fr-b11-n04: Prices on the menu already include tax by law, so the number is the number you pay — except that eating in is taxed higher than taking away.
fr-b11-p02: There are two of you and the place looks nearly full. Ask whether they have room. Speak now.
fr-b11-t02: 二人ですが、席はありますか？
fr-b11-p03: You are seated and nothing has been handed to you yet. Speak now.
fr-b11-t03: メニューをお願いします。
fr-b11-n06: Water and often tea come free, with a wet towel. Asking for more water is completely ordinary at any table.
fr-b11-p04: It is hot and your glass has been empty for a while. Speak now.
fr-b11-p05: Evening, and you want a single glass of the house red rather than a bottle. Speak now.
fr-b11-t05: 赤ワインをグラスでお願いします。
fr-b11-r02: 赤ワインですね。かしこまりました。お連れ様は？
fr-b11-n03: Onegai shimasu also carries an action as a noun: yoyaku o onegai shimasu, chumon o onegai shimasu — same ending, longer reach.
fr-b11-p06: You walk past a restaurant at noon and want to lock in a place before it fills. Speak now.
fr-b11-t06: 今夜、二人で予約をお願いします。
fr-b11-r03: 今夜は満席です。明日の夜八時はいかがですか？
fr-b11-p07: Lunchtime, and you want whatever the day's set is. Speak now.
fr-b11-t07: 日替わりはありますか？
fr-b11-n05: No tipping here; staff will run after you to return coins. A service charge, where it exists, is a posted line, not one you add.
fr-b11-p08: You decided five minutes ago and nobody has come back. Catch the next pass. Speak now.
fr-b11-p09: The person you are with just ordered something that sounded good and you want that too. Speak now.
fr-b11-t09: 同じものをお願いします。
fr-b11-n07: You call the staff with sumimasen, not a raised hand or a click. Sumimasen is the door; the order walks through it.
fr-b11-p10: You have just reached the counter and need to get someone's attention, then ask for two coffees. Speak now.
fr-b11-t10: すみません、コーヒーを二つお願いします。
fr-b11-s01: コーヒーをお願いします。メニューをお願いします。今夜の予約をお願いします。
fr-b11-n08: B11 done. Onegai shimasu carried a coffee, some water, a glass, the menu and tonight's booking.
fr-b11-q-i: A traveller names the thing, finishes with onegai shimasu, and gets the water and tea that cost nothing.
fr-b11-q01: コーヒーをお願いします。
fr-b11-q02: コーヒーですね。店内でお召し上がりですか？
fr-b11-q03: 店内で。お水もお願いします。
fr-b11-q04: かしこまりました。お水はサービスです。
fr-b12-n01: You can already order. This is the phrase that changes what actually arrives.
fr-b12-n02: The frame is the thing you do not want, then nuki de. Wasabi, ice, sauce, sugar — the ingredient first, then nuki de after it.
fr-b12-t01: わさび抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-p01: At the sushi counter you have just ordered, and the wasabi goes in by default between the fish and the rice. Speak now.
fr-b12-r01: わさび抜きですね。承知しました。
fr-b12-n03: Nuki de goes at the end of the order or stands alone. Wasabi nuki de is a complete sentence at a counter.
fr-b12-p02: At the café at breakfast you order a cola and you know the glass will come half full of cubes. Speak now.
fr-b12-t02: コーラを氷抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-p03: At the counter they are about to reach for the mayonnaise, which goes on almost everything here. Speak now.
fr-b12-t03: マヨネーズ抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-n04: Say it while ordering. Once a dish is built, a kitchen can move things around but not unmake them.
fr-b12-r02: ソースはもう入っています。別のお皿にしましょうか？
fr-b12-n06: Betsu de is the other half. Sauce betsu de means on the side instead of out; sukuname means a little less of it.
fr-b12-p04: He has just offered you a way to keep it separate, and you want to take it. Speak now.
fr-b12-t04: ソースは別でお願いします。
fr-b12-p05: Morning, café at breakfast, and you drink your tea plain. Speak now.
fr-b12-t05: 紅茶を砂糖抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-n05: Watch the stock. Dashi is fish, and it hides in dishes that look purely vegetable, so no meat is not the same as no fish.
fr-b12-p06: Back at the ramen counter, the bowl comes piled with spring onion you would rather skip. Speak now.
fr-b12-t06: ねぎ抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-p07: You are scanning a board of set meals and one whole family of them is out for you. Speak now.
fr-b12-t07: 豚肉抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-r03: それでしたら、鶏肉の定食はいかがですか？
fr-b12-p08: You cannot eat wheat. You are pointing at one dish and you need to know before you order it. Speak now.
fr-b12-t08: グルテン抜きはできますか？
fr-b12-n07: Okawari means a refill. It gets you more rice without building a new sentence, and it is often free.
fr-b12-p09: Your rice bowl is empty and there is still food on your plate. Speak now.
fr-b12-t09: ご飯のおかわり、お願いします。
fr-b12-n08: This is preference, not allergy. An allergy gets its own sentence and its own written card, in the next part.
fr-b12-p10: At the café counter you want the milky one, but not with dairy. Ask whether it can be done. Speak now.
fr-b12-t10: 乳製品抜きはできますか？
fr-b12-s01: わさび抜きで、お願いします。コーラを氷抜きで。紅茶を砂糖抜きで。
fr-b12-n09: B12 done. Nuki de took out the wasabi, the ice, the mayo, the sugar and the spring onion — the same two syllables every time.
fr-b12-q-i: A traveller edits one dish at the moment of ordering, and takes the on-the-side version when out is impossible.
fr-b12-q01: わさび抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b12-q02: わさび抜きですね。承知しました。ソースは？
fr-b12-q03: ソースは別でお願いします。魚介抜きはできますか？
fr-b12-q04: 厨房で聞いてきます。出汁は魚ですが、大丈夫ですか？
fr-b13-n01: Part thirteen. One sentence today has to land unmistakably. Everything else here hangs off it.
fr-b13-n02: The pad is open, three of you are ordering at once, and nobody has named what is in the stock or the sauce.
fr-b13-t01: ピーナッツアレルギーがあります。命に関わります。
fr-b13-n03: Two halves. The allergy, then how serious it is. The second half is what sends somebody to the kitchen.
fr-b13-p01: You have just sat down and the menus have not arrived. Say the peanut sentence, both halves. Speak now.
fr-b13-r01: 厨房で確認してきます。それまで注文しないでください。
fr-b13-n04: That reply is the one you want. The kitchen holds the list; the dining room does not.
fr-b13-p02: Somebody at the table is offering you a taste, just a small one. Draw the line in one sentence. Speak now.
fr-b13-t02: アレルギーで、好き嫌いではありません。
fr-b13-n05: Now the frame from part twelve does the rest of the work. The thing you cannot have, then nuki de.
fr-b13-p03: The waiter is back with the pen down on the pad. Repeat it as a rule for everything you order. Speak now.
fr-b13-t03: ピーナッツ抜きで、とても大切です。
fr-b13-p04: A bakery counter, and you are choosing for the person waiting outside. Speak now.
fr-b13-t04: 小麦抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b13-p05: A seafood restaurant, and half the board is shellfish. Set your condition before you choose. Speak now.
fr-b13-t05: 魚介抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b13-r02: 本日の定食には入っています。鶏肉のほうになさいますか？
fr-b13-p06: The dish you want comes with cream. Ask whether a version exists that does not. Speak now.
fr-b13-t06: 乳製品抜きはできますか？
fr-b13-n06: Three syllables widen it: dekimasu ka turns a flat no into a question the kitchen can go and solve.
fr-b13-p07: The vegetables arrive glossy and you can see why. Ask for the other version. Speak now.
fr-b13-t07: バター抜きはできますか？
fr-b13-p08: You are at a sweets counter choosing something for later. Set the condition. Speak now.
fr-b13-p09: A sandwich counter at a station, and the fillings are all in Japanese. State what you do not eat. Speak now.
fr-b13-t09: 豚肉抜きで、お願いします。
fr-b13-p10: A pastry is in front of you and the top layer is unidentifiable. Ask about the one thing you need to know. Speak now.
fr-b13-t10: これにナッツは入っていますか？
fr-b13-p11: The room is loud and you have said it twice already. Hand over the written version. Speak now.
fr-b13-t11: アレルギーのカードです。日本語で書いてあります。
fr-b13-n07: The card is the backup, never the opener. You say it out loud first, then hand it across.
fr-b13-p12: The answer you got was a shrug. Send the question to the person who cooked it. Speak now.
fr-b13-t12: 厨房で確認してもらえますか？
fr-b13-r03: 料理長が確認しました。こちらは大丈夫です。
fr-b13-n08: And the number, once, so it is already in your mouth: one one nine reaches fire and ambulance, one one zero the police. There is no 112 here.
fr-b13-p13: It is happening, and somebody near you has a phone in their hand. Give the instruction. Speak now.
fr-b13-t13: いちいちきゅうばんに電話してください。
fr-b13-n09: You are allowed to stop the ordering to say it. Saying it twice costs nothing and buys the whole meal.
fr-b13-s01: ピーナッツアレルギーがあります。命に関わります。ピーナッツ抜きで、とても大切です。厨房で確認してもらえますか？
fr-b13-n10: B13 done. The hammer sentence, nuki de plus the thing, the kitchen question, the card, and one one nine.
fr-b13-q-i: A traveller says the allergy sentence before the order is written, and the question goes to the kitchen.
fr-b13-q01: ピーナッツアレルギーがあります。命に関わります。
fr-b13-q02: 厨房で確認してきます。それまで注文しないでください。
fr-b13-q03: ピーナッツ抜きで、とても大切です。
fr-b13-q04: 料理長が確認しました。こちらは大丈夫です。
fr-b14-n01: Part fourteen. The bill, and the good news is that the arithmetic was done before you sat down.
fr-b14-n02: The bowls are gone, the counter is full behind you, and nothing happens next until you ask.
fr-b14-t01: お会計をお願いします。
fr-b14-p01: A member of staff passes your table carrying two glasses and catches your eye for half a second. Speak now.
fr-b14-r01: かしこまりました。お会計はあちらのレジでお願いします。
fr-b14-n03: Tax is inside the price here by law, and there is no tip. A service charge, where a place has one, is a posted line — not something you add.
fr-b14-p02: The place looks a little formal and you want to know if anything is added on top. Speak now.
fr-b14-t02: サービス料は入っていますか？
fr-b14-r02: うちはサービス料はありません。表示の金額だけです。
fr-b14-p03: Four of you, one slip, and somebody wants the figure out loud. Speak now.
fr-b14-n04: You pay at the register, not the table. The slip on your table is the 伝票 — carry it to the front and settle there.
fr-b14-p04: Dinner for three, and somebody at work is going to want the paperwork. Ask for the formal receipt. Speak now.
fr-b14-t04: 領収書をお願いします。
fr-b14-n05: Two papers: a レシート is the ordinary till slip, a 領収書 is the formal receipt for expenses. Ask for the 領収書 by name.
fr-b14-p05: You are at the register and your wallet only has plastic in it. Say how you are settling. Speak now.
fr-b14-t05: カードでお願いします。
fr-b14-r03: 申し訳ありません、当店は現金のみです。
fr-b14-n06: Cash always works; a card does not have to be taken. Cashless is spreading in the cities, but small places may still be cash only.
fr-b14-p06: You are at the door of a small place, before ordering, and there is no card sticker anywhere. Speak now.
fr-b14-p07: Two of you, two wallets, one slip. Say it before they start ringing it up as one. Speak now.
fr-b14-p08: One line on the slip is a figure you did not expect for the last round. Ask about that item. Speak now.
fr-b14-t08: コーヒーはいくらですか？
fr-b14-p09: The card machine beeps and they are about to bin the little slip. Speak now.
fr-b14-t09: レシートをお願いします。
fr-b14-p10: Two hours at that table, a good meal, and no tip is expected. Close it the way people close a meal here. Speak now.
fr-b14-n07: There is no percentage to work out and nothing extra is owed. The thing you leave behind is a sentence, not a coin.
fr-b14-s01: お会計をお願いします。全部でいくらですか？ カードでお願いします。
fr-b14-n08: B14 done. Ask for it, hear the total, name your method, take the receipt — and the tax was already in the number, with no tip on top.
fr-b14-q-i: A traveller closes a meal: asks for the bill, hears the total, names the method and carries the slip to the register.
fr-b14-q01: お会計をお願いします。
fr-b14-q02: かしこまりました。お会計はあちらのレジでお願いします。
fr-b14-q03: カードでお願いします。
fr-b14-q04: 申し訳ありません、当店は現金のみです。
fr-b15-n01: Part fifteen. One ending today, and it answers for you at an izakaya, a counter, a stall and a till.
fr-b15-n02: You are half onto a stool at an izakaya, they are already crossing towards you, and a small charged dish is about to land at your place.
fr-b15-n03: Here is the frame: the thing, then wa ikura desu ka. The ending holds; only what comes before it moves.
fr-b15-t01: お通しはいくらですか？
fr-b15-p01: You are one second from sitting at the izakaya and a small dish is coming you did not order. Ask before the stool takes your weight. Speak now.
fr-b15-r01: お通しは、お一人様三百円です。
fr-b15-n04: The otoshi is a small dish placed at your seat and charged per person — a legal cover, not a scam, even though you never ordered it.
fr-b15-p02: There is a small sign by the door you could not read. Ask about the seat charge before you commit. Speak now.
fr-b15-n05: Prices are easy to check first: they include tax, many windows show plastic food samples and photos, and set meals list the total.
fr-b15-p03: Standing outside, reading the board, and one line has no figure beside it. Speak now.
fr-b15-t03: 日替わり定食はいくらですか？
fr-b15-p04: At the market stall, your finger over a tray of something orange, no ticket anywhere on it. Speak now.
fr-b15-r02: 一パック三百円です。いくつにしますか？
fr-b15-p05: In the clothes shop, the jacket you like, and the only one on the rail is plainly too small. Speak now.
fr-b15-t05: 私のサイズはありますか？
fr-b15-p06: She has come back from the stockroom holding the right one. Ask for the next step. Speak now.
fr-b15-t06: 試着してもいいですか？
fr-b15-n06: In a small shop you open with sumimasen and ask second. Asking the price is not rude — it is the ordinary next word.
fr-b15-p07: Two almost identical things behind glass and one shared ticket between them. Point and ask. Speak now.
fr-b15-t07: こちらはいくらですか？
fr-b15-p08: You have heard the figure and you want it. Close the thing. Speak now.
fr-b15-p09: The till has no card stickers on it and you have only a few coins. Check before she wraps it. Speak now.
fr-b15-t09: カードで払ってもいいですか？
fr-b15-p10: Somebody has come over to help and you have not decided anything yet. Buy yourself the room. Speak now.
fr-b15-n07: Nobody behind a Japanese counter finds ikura desu ka odd, and nobody is marking how you phrased it.
fr-b15-n08: You have just priced the izakaya, the counter, the market stall and the clothes shop. Nobody gave you four questions — you kept one ending.
fr-b15-s01: お通しはいくらですか？ 日替わり定食はいくらですか？ これはいくらですか？
fr-b15-n09: B15 done. Ikura desu ka covers the cover dish, the set meal, the stall and the shop — always before you commit.
fr-b15-q-i: A traveller prices the seat before sitting in it, then takes the same ending to a stall and a shop.
fr-b15-q01: お通しはいくらですか？
fr-b15-q02: お通しは、お一人様三百円です。
fr-b15-q04: 一パック三百円です。いくつにしますか？
fr-b16-n01: Check-in is the cheapest minute of the whole stay. Ask now and it is a favour. Ask tomorrow and it is a move.
fr-b16-n02: Here is the frame: the thing, then sagashite imasu. It works even when you do not know the place has one.
fr-b16-t01: もっと静かな部屋を探しています。
fr-b16-p01: At the front desk, before the key is out of the drawer. There is a lift shaft the other side of that wall. Say what you are after. Speak now.
fr-b16-r01: かしこまりました。上の階に、静かなお部屋がございます。
fr-b16-n03: A higher floor, away from the street, is the quiet side — and that is what you were actually asking for.
fr-b16-p02: Still at the desk. The street below is a bus route and the window is thin. Ask whether anything is free higher up. Speak now.
fr-b16-t02: 上の階の部屋はありますか？
fr-b16-p03: It is eleven in the morning and the room is not ready until three. You want your hands free. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b16-t03: ここに荷物を置いてもいいですか？
fr-b16-r02: はい、フロントでお預かりします。番号札をお渡しします。
fr-b16-n04: Same frame, different counter. When you know the thing exists here, arimasu ka does the asking instead.
fr-b16-p04: Your data plan is nearly gone and there is no card on the desk with a password on it. Ask. Speak now.
fr-b16-t04: ワイファイはありますか？
fr-b16-p05: Half past seven, ground floor, three unmarked doors and a smell of coffee coming from one of them. Speak now.
fr-b16-t05: 朝食会場を探しています。
fr-b16-n05: Upstairs the frame keeps working, and the person with the cleaning cart in the corridor can solve most of it.
fr-b16-p06: In the corridor upstairs, housekeeping cart parked outside the next door. The room was colder than you expected. Speak now.
fr-b16-t06: もう一枚、毛布をもらってもいいですか？
fr-b16-p07: Back at the front desk. Your train is at six and the card in the room says eleven. Ask about the last morning. Speak now.
fr-b16-t07: レイトチェックアウトはありますか？
fr-b16-p08: On the street outside the hotel, asking the person locking up the shop next door. You have a few coins in your pocket. Speak now.

fr-i07-n03: Oishii, saiko, zeppin. All three are ordinary words here and all three beat a plain very good.
fr-i07-p02: Praise the house rather than the plate, on your way past the counter. Speak now.

fr-i07-t06: すみません、まだかかりますか？

fr-i08-n02: Then ask about bringing something. Rising voice at the end is the whole question — no extra words needed.

fr-i08-n04: One o'clock is a real hour. Mealtimes here are measured and fairly fixed, and the meal is built to run long.
fr-i08-p04: Everyone is standing around the table and nobody has sat down. Ask rather than choose your own seat. Speak now.

fr-i08-n05: The toast is one word, not a speech. Glasses up, kanpai, and that is genuinely the whole thing.

fr-i08-p06: Praise the food to the person who cooked it, pointing at the dish itself. Speak now.

fr-i08-t07: じゃあ、少しだけ。すごく美味しいので。
fr-i08-r04: もう、敬語じゃなくていいですよ。
fr-i08-n06: Tea is the signal. Once it has been served and drunk, leaving reads as normal rather than early.
fr-i08-p08: The tea cups are empty. Cover the whole afternoon in one sentence, still seated. Speak now.
fr-i08-t08: 今日は本当にありがとうございました。楽しい一日でした。

fr-i09-n01: A closed door here has a logic behind it. Knowing it turns the emptiest-looking day into the best one of the week.

fr-i09-n03: Each place keeps its own closing day, and museums mostly shut on Mondays. Check it before you walk twenty minutes to a dark door.

fr-i09-p03: You are at a stall with no idea what is in season. Hand the choice to the person selling. Speak now.
fr-i09-p04: There is something on the stall you have never seen. Ask before committing to half a kilo of it. Speak now.
fr-i09-t04: 味見してもいいですか？
fr-i09-r03: どうぞ、味見してください。切りますね。
fr-i09-p05: Order a small amount — lunch for two people, today, not a week of it. Speak now.

fr-i09-n05: Then the afternoon. Ask a local what they do on a day off: the answer is a plan, and it beats the guidebook.
fr-i09-p06: Ask the person behind the stall about their own day off, not about attractions. Speak now.

fr-i09-p08: There is one free bench and somebody's bag on the next one. Ask. Speak now.
fr-i09-t08: ここに座ってもいいですか？
fr-i09-p09: The shop is open today but you do not know how late. Ask before you plan around it. Speak now.

fr-i10-n01: Four money questions come up on every trip, and all four are answered by a sign on a wall or a number on the tag.
fr-i10-n02: First: there is no tip. Cash handed over on top is usually declined, and no percentage is waiting at the end.
fr-i10-t01: サービス料はかかりますか？
fr-i10-p01: The bill is in front of you and you are wondering whether anything gets added on top. Ask instead. Speak now.
fr-i10-r01: いいえ、税込価格です。チップも要りませんよ。
fr-i10-n03: The warm close is words, not coins. Gochisosama deshita does the work a tip does elsewhere; a gratuity is often refused.
fr-i10-p02: Lunch was long and good and you have paid the exact figure. Close it warmly, the way people do here. Speak now.
fr-i10-t02: ごちそうさまでした。美味しかったです。
fr-i10-n04: Second: nobody must take your card, and a cash-only sign or a minimum is lawful. Cashless is spreading, but not everywhere.
fr-i10-r02: カードは三千円からになります。
fr-i10-p03: There is a sticker by the register and you cannot read the figure on it. Ask for the number. Speak now.
fr-i10-t03: 最低金額はいくらですか？
fr-i10-n05: The condition is posted before you order: a sign at the door, at the register, or on the ticket machine.
fr-i10-p04: You are still in the doorway with nothing ordered yet. Settle it now. Speak now.
fr-i10-p05: He has just pointed at the sign. Give him the easy answer and keep the meal. Speak now.
fr-i10-t05: じゃあ、現金で払います。
fr-i10-n06: Cash is the one they cannot turn down. Yen is legal tender, and that part is not the shop's to decide.
fr-i10-p06: The purchase is three hundred yen and the machine only gave you ten-thousand notes. Say so before the drawer opens. Speak now.
fr-i10-t06: 一万円札でもいいですか？
fr-i10-n07: Third: the tag price is the price you pay. Since 2021 it must be shown tax-included, so nothing is added at the register.
fr-i10-p07: Three of you ordered, one of you is paying, and you want the whole figure first. Speak now.
fr-i10-n08: Fourth: splitting. Betsubetsu at the register is ordinary here, and asking for it costs you nothing.
fr-i10-p08: Two of you at the register, two cards out, one bill on the tray. Speak now.
fr-i10-p09: The register beeps, the drawer shuts, and nothing prints. You need proof for the expense claim. Speak now.
fr-i10-t09: レシートをお願いします。
fr-i10-s01: カードで払えますか？ 最低金額はいくらですか？ じゃあ、現金で払います。

fr-a01-n01: So far, Japanese aimed at you. This part is Japanese aimed at somebody else — a different thing entirely.
fr-a01-n02: Rule one: the desu and masu drop. Wakarimasen is what gets said to you. Wakannai is what they say to each other.
fr-a01-n03: Same idea, three sizes: wakarimasen, wakaranai, wakannai. All three are ordinary speech, and only the first is for you.
fr-a01-r02: 見てないの？何もないよ、別に。
fr-a01-n04: The particles go too. Iru becomes teru, and the wo and the ga simply vanish. You only ever need to spot these, never to say them.
fr-a01-r03: そろそろ行かなきゃ。もう遅いし。
fr-a01-n05: Rule two: a few very small words carry the traffic — ne, sa, maa, nanka, tte iu ka. Catch those and the rest opens.
fr-a01-r04: まあね、うん。そういうこと。
fr-a01-n06: Ne checks you are still there. Sa keeps the floor. Maa softens. Nanka is a spoken um, and tte iu ka means or rather.
fr-a01-r05: で、どうする？っていうか、まだ決めてないんだけど。
fr-a01-n07: De at the front opens a consequence — so, then. Kedo at the end trails off and softens. Both are filler and both arrive constantly.
fr-a01-r06: えっと、全部で三千八百円ね。
fr-a01-n08: Prices come out as one block. Watch the little screen instead of doing arithmetic in a second language.
fr-a01-r07: 元気にしてた？ほな、こっち座りいな。
fr-a01-n09: A regional accent is not another language. Name it as Kansai in your head and the worry about your own ear drops.
fr-a01-r08: まあ、じゃあ行こっか。うん、それで決まりね。
fr-a01-n10: English here is limited and patchy. Expect it at travel counters and big hotels, and expect to work in Japanese most other places.
fr-a01-p01: You caught nothing at all. Say so once, cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
fr-a01-x01: すみません、わかりませんでした。
fr-a01-p02: Ask for the whole thing again, you just need a second pass. Speak now.
fr-a01-x02: もう一度お願いします。
fr-a01-p03: The second pass was the same speed as the first. Ask for the one thing that would fix it. Speak now.
fr-a01-x03: もっとゆっくりお願いします。
fr-a01-p04: One word in the middle did all the work and you missed it. Point at it and ask. Speak now.
fr-a01-x04: それ、どういう意味ですか？
fr-a01-p05: It is a place name and hearing it a third time will not help. Ask for it on paper. Speak now.
fr-a01-p06: You got the gist and lost the detail. Say exactly that, so they repeat the useful half. Speak now.
fr-a01-x06: だいたいわかりましたが、全部は…
fr-a01-p07: They switched to English to help, the queue is empty and you would rather keep going. Ask. Speak now.
fr-a01-x07: 日本語で続けてもいいですか？
fr-a01-p08: The table has just turned from you to each other, and you lost the thread. Say what you noticed, cheerfully. Speak now.
fr-a01-x08: お二人だと、ずっと速いですね！
fr-a01-s01: すみません、わかりませんでした。もう一度お願いします。もっとゆっくりお願いします。
fr-a01-n11: A01 done. The desu and masu go, plain form takes over, a few small words carry the meaning, and a third of the room is plenty.
fr-a01-q-i: Two people settle a plan at full speed, and a traveller catches the shape of it.
fr-a01-q01: さあ、わかんないなあ。もう遅いし。
fr-a01-q02: そろそろ行かなきゃ。八時過ぎたら何もないよ。
fr-a01-q03: まあ、じゃあ行こっか。それで決まりね。
fr-a01-q04: すみません、わかりませんでした。もっとゆっくりお願いします。
fr-a02-n01: Humour is the last thing a language hands you and the first thing that misfires. This part is mostly listening.
fr-a02-n02: The rhythm that dominates is the tsukkomi: a flat, sharp-sounding correction thrown at a friend. It sounds like a jab and means closeness.
fr-a02-r01: はいはい、すごいすごい。よく言うわ。
fr-a02-n03: Sugoi, honto, saikou — said with no lift at all, they can mean the reverse. Listen to the flatness, not the word.
fr-a02-r02: へえ、そうなんだ。ふーん。
fr-a02-n04: Second: the tease between people with history. It sounds far harder than it is meant, and it closes with a laugh.
fr-a02-r03: もう、何言ってんの！…なんてね、冗談冗談。
fr-a02-n05: Nante ne, joudan joudan, uso uso — three ways of saying that was a joke. All three mean closeness, not distance.
fr-a02-r04: ちょっと聞いてや、昨日な、面白いことあってん。
fr-a02-n06: That kind of bit belongs to the people who share the reference. A visitor performing one is not joining in — it lands as a verdict.
fr-a02-r05: まあ、東京と大阪はな、もう別もんやから。
fr-a02-p01: The table has turned to you for a verdict on their own regional argument. Decline it, cheerfully. Speak now.
fr-a02-x01: いやあ、そこはノーコメントで！
fr-a02-n07: That line is worth memorising. It gets a laugh, it costs nothing, and it keeps you out of every old regional argument.
fr-a02-n08: So what is yours? Make yourself the subject: your Japanese, your chopsticks, the ramen you have eaten every single day.
fr-a02-p02: Get in first about your own Japanese, before anyone else has to be polite about it. Speak now.
fr-a02-x02: 私の日本語、下手ですみません。
fr-a02-r06: いやいや、日本語お上手ですよ。
fr-a02-p03: Confess, proudly, what you have eaten every single day of this trip. Speak now.
fr-a02-x03: 毎日ラーメンを食べました。後悔してません。
fr-a02-r07: 餃子も毎回頼んでたでしょ？正直に！
fr-a02-p04: Own it instead of explaining yourself, and raise the number. Speak now.
fr-a02-x04: はい、犯人です。二杯食べました。
fr-a02-n09: That is the whole move. Being teased and agreeing cheerfully is how a table stops handling you carefully.
fr-a02-p05: You got there half a beat late, but you got there. Show it without explaining it. Speak now.
fr-a02-p06: Name the joke out loud and admit how long it took you. It always gets a laugh. Speak now.
fr-a02-x06: 今の、冗談ですね。三秒かかりました。
fr-a02-p07: Everyone laughed and you have no idea why. Ask, instead of doing the polite laugh. Speak now.
fr-a02-x07: 今の冗談、わからなかったです。教えてください。
fr-a02-p08: Somebody teased you and you liked it. Say so and hand them the point. Speak now.
fr-a02-x08: 笑わせてくれますね。そのとおりです。
fr-a02-s01: 私の日本語、下手ですみません。はい、犯人です。二杯食べました。そこはノーコメントで！
fr-a02-n10: A02 done. Flat can mean inverted, the teasing is theirs, the regional argument is theirs, and the joke about you is yours.
fr-a02-q-i: A table teases, a traveller agrees cheerfully, and stays out of the old argument.
fr-a02-q01: はいはい、すごいすごい。よく言うわ。
fr-a02-q02: 毎日ラーメンでしょ？正直に！
fr-a02-q03: はい、犯人です。二杯食べました。
fr-a02-q04: いやあ、そこはノーコメントで！
fr-a03-n01: Every country tells a story about itself. A lot of this one sits on a table, at a fixed hour, and changes with the season.
fr-a03-r01: うちはね、パソコンの前では食べないの。ちゃんと座ってね。
fr-a03-n02: Lunch has an hour rather than a window, and many kitchens shut between services. That shapes your whole day.
fr-a03-n03: This part is measured. Time-use surveys show mealtimes here bunched tight — lunch around noon, dinner in the early evening, everyone at once.
fr-a03-p01: The room emptied at two and you want to know when it fills again. Ask the person clearing the table. Speak now.
fr-a03-t01: お昼は何時に食べますか？
fr-a03-r02: お昼は十二時ごろ、みんないっせいに来ますよ。
fr-a03-n04: There is a law defining a food label — the GI mark — tying a product to a place and a method, with a registered symbol attached.
fr-a03-p02: A dish on the board looks good and you want to know how it got to the plate. Ask. Speak now.
fr-a03-r03: うちは全部手作りです。お味噌だけは近所の蔵のを使ってますけど。
fr-a03-n05: The GI mark is voluntary, so no mark proves nothing. Asking beats hunting for a symbol on the menu.
fr-a03-p03: You want the thing this town claims as its own, not the thing on every menu in the country. Ask. Speak now.
fr-a03-t03: この辺の名物は何ですか？
fr-a03-r04: ここはやっぱりお蕎麦ですね。よそとは出汁が違うんですよ。
fr-a03-n06: Now the other half of the story: the running joke people here make about themselves.
fr-a03-r05: 日本人はね、すぐ「すみません」って謝るんですよ。癖でね。
fr-a03-n07: The same goes for the this-town-used-to-be-quieter line. Agreeing with it is the one move that lands badly.
fr-a03-r06: 昔はもっと静かな町だったんですけどねえ。
fr-a03-p04: They have just told you it was all better before. Do not agree and do not argue — ask them. Speak now.
fr-a03-t04: この町、何が変わりましたか？
fr-a03-p05: They name something everyone here grew up with and you have never heard of it. Say so and hand them the floor. Speak now.
fr-a03-t05: 知らないので、教えてください。
fr-a03-r07: ああ、それはね、話すと長いですよ。まあ座って。
fr-a03-p06: The meal was better than you expected. Say it as your own experience, without comparing it to anywhere. Speak now.
fr-a03-t06: ここで、とてもおいしくいただきました。本当に。
fr-a03-p07: They used a word for the dish that you want to keep. Ask for it, pointing at the plate. Speak now.
